text: It is believed that Egil lived at Mosfell from the year A.D. 974-990. In about 990 Egil dies and is buried at Tjaldanes, south of Hrísbrú. When Grim Svertingsson built his church at Hrísbrú in the year 1000, as stated in Egils Saga, Thordis took up Egils bones and moved them to the church. Magnus Guðmundsson says that some people think that the farm of Hrísbrú was formerly named Mosfell, but that changes to the place names took place later. Egils Saga says that the church was taken down in the year 1150 and that could also hold true for the excavated church at Hrísbrú. Egils Saga says that the bones of Egil were exhumed and moved to Mosfell because it was required by the Christian Law in Grágás [Medieval Icelandic Law] that burials be moved along with churches. Magnús says that it is impossible to tell whether the bones of Egil are among those that have been found during the archaeological excavations: We do not know that. They have found large bones in a box besides the church, but it is very difficult to determine whether they are the bones of Egil. We are all descendents of Egil and, who knows, we Icelanders might even be able to take a DNA test to see if some of us are related to this newly excavated person. Egils Saga says, on the other hand, that the bones of Egil were removed and placed on the outskirts of the churchyard at Mosfell says Magnús. Morgunblaðið 5. ágúst 2004
